Implications of changes were described in all records where relevant. One pilot impact study completed and two more initiated by end 2023.Each database record documenting new upcoming and amended EU regulatory and nonregulatory measures includes an assessment of potential implications for partner countries. Recommended actions to be taken by partner countries to align with the changes are also made when possible and relevant. This information is based on literature review and consultation with key stakeholders. A pilot study was completed in 2023 to test and refine the proposed AGRINFO impact assessment methodology. Two further studies were commissioned and initiated in 2023.

comment.narrative: Potential social economic and environmental impacts from at least 15 regulatorynonregulatory measures are actively disseminated towards all relevant stakeholders during the life of the programme

Implications of changes were described in all records where relevant. One pilot impact study completed and two more initiated by end 2023.Uptodate information available from public access database. Regular newsletter issued to 3000 subscribers highlighting key changes 17. Email alerts for critical changes 8. Prototype country regulatory digest developed and webinars on request 6.During 2023 AGRINFO worked to build a network and partner beneficiary contact list an activity that will continue throughout the life of the programme. The focus was on establishing operational links with organisations that act as relays to transfer information to endusers Brussels embassies and trade missions EU Delegations national partner beneficiaries. These efforts ensured that by end2023 there were 3000 subscribers to the AGRINFO newsletter issued every 23 weeks to highlight key changes 17 during 2023. 8 alerts were sent by email warning countriessectors concerned of critical and timesensitive changes. 6 webinars were held on request to demonstrate the service and provide information on specific topics. A quarterly country digest was prepared at the request of Cote dIvoire providing a template for replication in other priority countries.

comment.narrative: AGRINFO operates a monitoring protocol and a workflow for filtering writing reviewing editing and publishing records. During 2023 it has produced consistent and highquality content. Over 180 new records were added to the database during 2023 giving a total of 340 records by the end of the reporting period. These cover all policy and regulatory changes published since August 2022 relevant to agrifood and fish exports from AGRINFO partner countries as well as 30 explainer documents that give a background to the context regulatory framework and briefs on key EU policy initiatives. During 2023 in response to user feedback a template was developed to provide summarised content short records to facilitate transmission of information by relay organisations to end users.

description.narrative: IOV 1.7. Sustainabilityrelated changes to trade agreements with the EU in the agricultural sector are identified and documented

comment.narrative: 100 of changes are identified and documented each year

AGRINFO monitors and documents relevant developments in trade policy trade defence trade negotiations and market access rules. During 2023 content for inclusion in the database was developed on all EU trade policies and trade agreements relevant to the scope of the programme. The decision was taken not to routinely provide updates on trade negotiations as these are covered by DG Trade websites and there is little scope for AGRINFO to add value. Instead from Q4 of this reporting period onwards a quarterly digest of trade policy developments is prepared and made available in the database.

description.narrative: IOV 1.7. Sustainabilityrelated changes to trade agreements with the EU in the agricultural sector are identified and documented

comment.narrative: 100 of changes are identified and documented each year

AGRINFO monitors and documents relevant developments in trade policy trade defence trade negotiations and market access rules. During 2023 content for inclusion in the database was developed on all EU trade policies and trade agreements relevant to the scope of the programme. The decision was taken not to routinely provide updates on trade negotiations as these are covered by DG Trade websites and there is little scope for AGRINFO to add value. Instead from Q4 of this reporting period onwards a quarterly digest of trade policy developments is prepared and made available in the database.

title.narrative: IOV 2.2 Changes to regulatory and nonregulatory measures and policies, and changes to trading conditions and rules identified under Result 1, are prioritised, and areas of concern and opportunities identified.

description.narrative: IOV 2.2 Changes to regulatory and nonregulatory measures and policies, and changes to trading conditions and rules identified under Result 1, are prioritised, and areas of concern and opportunities identified.

comment.narrative: The prioritisation methodology was further developed and improved during Period 2 and listings of priority countries generated from Q3 onwards. The methodology now combines UN development data with EU and IMF trade data to capture economic and social vulnerability from a development perspective and reliance on agrifood trade with the EU with a more robust dataset based on threeyear trade averages. The combined data provides a single figure to indicate sensitivity of countries to potential EU policy changes. This indicator is increasingly used to justify AGRINFO market analysis activities and to prioritise outreach. Feedback from the contracting party helped to orientate the approach which is now being used to prioritise countries and sectors on a regional basis. The African regional study was completed by the end of 2023 and the Latin America and Asia studies initiated. Target to be reviewed with the contracting party so that it is aligned with publication of the relevant UNEUIMF data updates.

title.narrative: IOV 2.3 Impact assessments are conducted on main areas of concern and opportunities, to understand practical consequences and potential needs for support

description.narrative: IOV 2.3 Impact assessments are conducted on main areas of concern and opportunities, to understand practical consequences and potential needs for support

comment.narrative: At least 15 impact assessments conducted and documented over the life of the programme

An expost impact assessment of the new EU Plant Health Law Regulation EU 20162031 in Kenya was initiated in December 2022 and completed during 2023. This was a pilot study and the experienced used to further refine the methodology. Selection of topics for study in 2023 was conducted in consultation with the contracting party and where relevant Commission services this creates some restrictions in terms of scope and timing affecting the ability of AGRINFO to deliver on the indicators as planned. Two further impact studies were initiated in 2023 to be completed in 2024 and a fourth is in the pipeline.

title.narrative: IOV 2.4 Qualitative and quantitative market analyses and profiles are conducted on agricultural value chains identified as main areas of concern and opportunities

description.narrative: IOV 2.4 Qualitative and quantitative market analyses and profiles are conducted on agricultural value chains identified as main areas of concern and opportunities

comment.narrative: At least 15 market analyses conducted and documented over the life of the programme

A framework has been developed and refined for the implementation of qualitative and quantitative market analyses. These are conducted on demand to support impact studies or to further analyse countries or sectors that are identified as particularly vulnerable to potential EU policy changes by the AGRINFO prioritisation process. During 2023 a market analysis was conducted in support of the impact study on increased controls under EU Regulation Regulation 20191793. A second analysis was conducted on coffee value chains recognised to be particularly vulnerable to forthcoming EU regulatory changes.

description.narrative: IOV 2.5 EU market access challenges and opportunities are translated into practical sectoral analyses, by target group, for the most directly affected agricultural value chains in partner countries

comment.narrative: At least 15 value chains are subject to sectoral analysis over the life of the programme

The approach to the sectoral analyses has been clarified in discussions with the contracting party. These guidance documents provide information on an item of EU policy giving more detail that can be included in an AGRINFO database record. They are targeted towards a specific sector with the aim of promoting greater practical understanding of the detailed requirements orientated towards those responsible for compliance. Following the plant health impact study in Kenya a guidance document on the export of capsicum to the EU was prepared in 2023. This also serves as a model for future documents.

title.narrative: IOV 3.1. Main beneficiaries are informed of new, upcoming and amended EU market access challenges, key areas of concern, and opportunities

description.narrative: IOV 3.1. Main beneficiaries are informed of new, upcoming and amended EU market access challenges, key areas of concern, and opportunities

comment.narrative: Listing of changes and main areas of concern and opportunities are actively disseminated e.g. newsletter information sessions to at least 100 direct beneficiaries biannually from Period 2

3000 subscribers representing diverse countries and entities receiving the AGRINFO newsletter 17 issues circulated during 2023. 8 email alerts to targeted partner beneficiaries. 6 webinar information sessions. The first newsletter AGRINFO Update was issued on 3rd February 2023 and thereafter sent regularly with a total of 17 during Period 2. The number of subscribers receiving the Update reached over 3000 by the end of the year. The newsletter highlights latest EU policies regulations information and feedback opportunities giving links to the full reports in the database. The intention is that direct beneficiaries and partners relay entities will forward relevant extracts to end users. The Ask AGRINFO service was launched in 2023 and received some 25 enquiries. 6 webinar information sessions were organised each followed by a QA. When necessary queries were clarified with the relevant Commission Services.

description.narrative: IOV 3.2. On a demandled basis, locally adapted information packs for partner countries are developed, and/or value chain/ country impact assessments are conducted

comment.narrative: At least 50 of demands are addressed through the provision of customised information

A request was received from the Ministry of Agriculture Cote dIvoire relayed by their Embassy in Brussels for more help to identify regulations that are relevant to them. After some interaction to better clarify their needs and requirements a template was prepared for a quarterly regulatory digest. Information is extracted from the database on all regulations relevant to their main agrifood and fish exports and compiled into an easytouse report. The first edition was prepared by late 2023 and issued in January 2024. From Period 3 this model can be offered to other high priority countriesvalue chains.

title.narrative: IOV 3.3. The intervention contributes directly to EU policy, legislative and standardsetting processes via public consultations, impact assessments, or other available route

description.narrative: IOV 3.3. The intervention contributes directly to EU policy, legislative and standardsetting processes via public consultations, impact assessments, or other available route

comment.narrative: At least 8 EU policy and legislative process to which the intervention contributes over the life of the programme

Information provided to partner countries on opportunities to give feedback to EU and WTO consultation on a continual basis. 1 response by COLEAD to official EU consultation.The main contribution made by AGRINFO is to provide partner countries with information on policy changes at an early stage and to highlight and facilitate opportunities for them to feed into EU or WTO consultation. Such opportunities are included in every AGRINFO newsletter. Where relevant information on specific consultation is also communicated proactively via email. For example in June 2023 the EU opened a public consultation call for evidence on stopping EU export of banned chemicals including pesticides. AGRINFO raised awareness among partner beneficiaries and shared links to the questionnaire for nonEU stakeholders. Information was also provided to COLEAD who submitted an official response. An explainer record was prepared on How to provide feedback on upcoming EU policies and regulations together with an overview of Upcoming EU regulatory changes and opportunities for feedback SeptemberDecember 2023 the latter will be updated quarterly. Target to be reviewed with the contracting party so that it is more appropriate to the approach in use.

description.narrative: IOV 3.3. The intervention contributes directly to EU policy, legislative and standardsetting processes via public consultations, impact assessments, or other available route

comment.narrative: At least 8 EU policy and legislative process to which the intervention contributes over the life of the programme

Information provided to partner countries on opportunities to give feedback to EU and WTO consultation on a continual basis. 1 response by COLEAD to official EU consultation.The main contribution made by AGRINFO is to provide partner countries with information on policy changes at an early stage and to highlight and facilitate opportunities for them to feed into EU or WTO consultation. Such opportunities are included in every AGRINFO newsletter. Where relevant information on specific consultation is also communicated proactively via email. For example in June 2023 the EU opened a public consultation call for evidence on stopping EU export of banned chemicals including pesticides. AGRINFO raised awareness among partner beneficiaries and shared links to the questionnaire for nonEU stakeholders. Information was also provided to COLEAD who submitted an official response. An explainer record was prepared on How to provide feedback on upcoming EU policies and regulations together with an overview of Upcoming EU regulatory changes and opportunities for feedback SeptemberDecember 2023 the latter will be updated quarterly. Target to be reviewed with the contracting party so that it is more appropriate to the approach in use.
